proposal.description_long: On February 17, 1999, the Washington Post reported that Evercore Partners had agreed to acquire American Media Inc., the Florida-based publisher of the National Enquirer and Star. The reported transaction included Evercore assuming American Media’s debt. David Pecker, then chief executive of Hachette Filipacchi Magazines, was hired to become American Media’s chairman and chief executive. The distinction between buying the publisher and taking its top job matters: the transaction was led by Evercore, while Pecker became the executive responsible for running the company. The record’s earlier title incorrectly described Pecker as personally buying the National Enquirer and called the publication Mafia-owned. The cited 1999 acquisition report does not support either assertion. It also does not establish a Trump-related purpose or connection in the transaction itself. Pecker’s later relationship with Donald Trump should not be projected backward onto this corporate change. The revised description is limited to the ownership transaction and Pecker’s appointment, both reported at the time. Separate evidence would be required for the publication’s earlier financing history or for any later political relationship involving its leadership.
